first_impression.reaction: I googled 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' because my mum keeps saying 'just use a travel agent' and I wanted to know if that's actually different. The opening tells me they're both just labels and to 'compare the service, not the title'. As a lawyer I appreciate that, it's honest and it saves me reading ten listicles that pretend there's a clean answer. It's also a bit deflating: I came for a verdict and got homework. But the homework is good. The side-by-side questions and the written-answers point are things I can actually use. No fairytale talk, no shouting. I skimmed the insurance part, read the Wedded Wonderland section properly, and would send the table to James and my parents.

journey.quote: So compare the service, not the title.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it reframes the question well. Still, I wanted at least a sense of when one tends to suit better than the other. It feels slightly like the question I asked got handed back to me.

journey.section: Is the honeymoon straight after the wedding, or later?
journey.quote: A honeymoon that leaves the morning after a destination wedding shares flights, dates and luggage with the wedding itself.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is exactly our situation if we go overseas, and nobody else writing about this mentions the luggage. Feels like someone who has actually done it.

journey.section: How many moving parts does the trip have?
journey.quote: Count the stops, flights, time zones and bookings that depend on each other: that is the coordination you are asking for.
journey.reaction: Useful. That's a practical way to work out what 'end-to-end' needs to mean for us, instead of taking anyone's word for it.

journey.section: Do you work across suppliers, or with a set list?
journey.quote: Then ask whether they receive anything from the suppliers they recommend, and whether that is disclosed to you.
journey.reaction: Good. Hidden costs are my biggest worry and commissions are the hidden cost no one talks about. Now I want Wedded Wonderland's own answer.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
journey.reaction: Every row in both columns is word-for-word identical. I read it twice thinking I'd missed the difference. I get the point (same questions for both), but two columns that say the same thing looks like a mistake rather than a message.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: Who will we deal with from first call to return?
journey.reaction: This is the one that matters to me. Someone accountable when things go wrong, not a call centre.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: Will the quote be in Australian dollars, with your fee shown separately from the trip?
journey.reaction: Exactly what I'd want to hold a planner to. Currency surprises with a European wedding are a real fear for us.

journey.section: Questions about what happens when plans change
journey.quote: An agent or intermediary is usually bound by the provider's terms and, legally, may only need to pass on the remedy that provider offers.
journey.reaction: That's genuinely useful and I didn't know it. It tells me who's actually on the hook.

journey.section: What does our travel insurance need to cover?
journey.quote: Read the Product Disclosure Statement for what is covered and what is excluded.
journey.reaction: Sensible but this is Smartraveller territory. I skimmed. The insolvency point is the only bit that ties back to choosing a planner or agent.

journey.quote: Wedded Wonderland is both in one relationship, so you never have to explain your wedding to someone who has not planned it, or your travel to someone who has not moved guests overseas.
journey.reaction: This is the line that speaks to us. One relationship for the wedding and the honeymoon, and someone who has moved guests overseas, which is our grandparents' airport problem.

journey.quote: We plan venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Every planner says 'anywhere in the world'. On a page that tells me to ask who they actually work with, I'd like to see it backed by one real honeymoon or wedding. It also doesn't answer the page's own question about whether they receive anything from suppliers.

journey.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor about the wedding, the honeymoon and the feeling you want, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see each inclusion on paper before you commit.
journey.reaction: Calm, no pressure. Fee in writing first is reassuring. Not enough on its own for me to enquire yet.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
turn_offs_found.why: Two columns with identical wording in every row reads like a copy-paste error. If the point is 'ask both the same thing', one column of questions plus 'why it matters' would say it more cleanly and look more polished.

turn_offs_found.quote: We plan venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Anywhere in the world' is the kind of claim every planner makes. Without proof nearby it slightly undercuts the careful, specific tone of the rest of the page.

would_share_with: My parents, who are contributing and keep suggesting a travel agent: the side-by-side questions, so we all ask the same things whoever we talk to
James: the 'When the honeymoon follows a destination wedding' section, because one plan or two is the decision we actually need to make

cta_reaction.quote: To start, [meet your Wedded Advisor through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planner-vs-travel-agent&utm_content=secondary).
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and one advisor, fee in writing, AUD quotes is what we want. But we're 14 months out with no destination, and I don't enquire until I've read a couple of posts and seen a real wedding I can picture. I'd click through to look at the Concierge page, not to enquire today.

top_3_changes: Fix the side-by-side table: the 'Ask a planner' and 'Ask an agent' columns are identical in every row, which reads as an error. Either collapse to one 'Ask everyone' column plus 'Why it matters', or add a line above the table saying the columns match on purpose because the labels overlap.

Give the intro a clearer payoff for people who came for a verdict: after 'So compare the service, not the title.', say plainly that this guide won't crown a winner and will instead show how to tell which service suits your trip, so it reads as a promise rather than a sidestep.

Tighten 'What does our travel insurance need to cover?' to the points that bear on choosing a planner or agent (timing and insolvency), and lean on the Smartraveller link for the rest, because it reads like a generic checklist and slows the page.

open_questions.question: Are the identical 'Ask a planner' and 'Ask an agent' columns intentional? If so, can a one-line explanation be added, or the table collapsed to a single question column?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' while early in destination wedding research, so relevance is 3 (honeymoon is secondary to the wedding for now) and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
The lack of industry generalisations, figures, fee model, commissions and proof is a deliberate deferral and is not penalised as a must-fix.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, key takeaways, the self-questions, the 'what they will do' questions, the table, the payment questions, the destination wedding and Wedded Wonderland sections, the FAQ and the close, with a skim of the insurance section.
